_doc: WED-ACQ2 / P1.7 automatic corpus expansion (records/wed-acq2-auto-corpus-expansion-plan.md). Read by vera/acq_config.py. The feature is OFF unless `enabled` is exactly true AND the kill-switch env var is not true-like AND both DB env vars are set. Env var NAMES only; values are never read except to build engines and never logged.
_calibration_note: Capacity and cost bounds below are planner priors (not decision thresholds). The only decision gate (relevance) reuses config/fulldoc_answer.json admission thresholds unchanged. Calibrate from the first live job log lines (reason-code counts and stage durations only) - plan DV-2.

_constraint.what: acquired documents are served without per-document pins (vera/fulldoc_db.py _load_acquired strips pins)
_constraint.condition: owner-run pin export before 2026-11-21, otherwise the extension lapses on 2026-11-21
_constraint.extended_by: OD-1109-HD1 (2026-11-09; the export does not close the vulnerability; H1(b) batch promotion retained)

question_text: VERA-DAR automatic acquisition (open-access full text; visitor question not stored)
_licence_hold_observations_note: LICENCE-ALLOWLIST-1104 (coordinator 2026-11-04): an UNKNOWN licence held on the full-text path is appended to licence_observations (reason_code licence_unknown) via the write-only account before the hold; false = not recorded.

triggers._note: plan s11 V1: classifier_malformed never triggers; layer-1 injection/deny patterns are re-run on the question before enqueue

scope_expansion._dar1021_note: DAR-1021: a layer-2 decline starts acquisition (and, only when override_layer2_declines is true, may later be answered from acquired documents alone through the unchanged full-document admission, claim check and citation path) ONLY when the classifier's category is in layer2_categories_allowed (closed enum; missing or unknown = no). Layer-1 declines, malformed replies, other categories and layer2_none never acquire or answer. UNCALIBRATED: the classifier's category accuracy has not been measured on live traffic.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note: VERA-DAR found and added these documents while answering this question.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_background_persist: VERA-DAR has tried every search available for this question. {n} source(s) it found but could not finish now may be checked later, but this is not guaranteed, and this answer will not update.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_background_persist_stopped: VERA-DAR stopped searching before every search option was tried ({reason}). {n} source(s) it found but could not finish now may be checked later, but this is not guaranteed, and this answer will not update.
scope_expansion._inline_notice_background_persist_note: MIDTERMS-WP8-1106 (owner OD-1106-MIDTERMS-D1D4, D1; review F1): keep-searching requests only, shown only when sources were actually handed to the best-effort background queue ({n} = that hand-off count; nothing is claimed as running). The 'tried every search' text is used only when the rounds stopped because every search variant was tried (acquisition.stop variants_exhausted); any other stop uses the _stopped text, whose {reason} is a fixed need-to-know phrase (vera.inline_acquire._STOP_REASON_TEXT). Same as the code defaults.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_stored: VERA-DAR answered from open-access documents it had already added to its collection for an earlier question.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_answer_only: VERA-DAR found these documents while answering this question and used them for this answer only; they had too few relevant passages to be added to its collection.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_mixed: VERA-DAR answered from documents it found or already held; some of the documents it found while answering this question had too few relevant passages to be added to its collection and were used for this answer only.
scope_expansion.inline_answer_note_unsaved: VERA-DAR found these documents while answering this question; they could not be saved to its collection.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_none: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but none passed its licence, content and relevance checks.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_deadline: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not finish checking them within its time limit.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_search_failed: VERA-DAR tried to search for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but the search did not complete.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_capped: VERA-DAR could not search for open-access full-text documents on this question right now because its hourly or daily search limit has been reached; no background search was started. Please try again later.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_doc_cap: VERA-DAR searched for open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not check new documents because its daily document limit has been reached; no background search was started.
scope_expansion.inline_notice_unanswered: VERA-DAR searched for and checked open-access full-text documents on this question while answering, but could not produce a checked answer from them.
scope_expansion.override_answer_prefix: The answer below comes only from open-access documents VERA-DAR added to its collection automatically after licence, content and relevance checks; it may be wrong. For medical, legal, financial or safety matters, please consult a qualified professional or an appropriate official source.
scope_expansion._note: plan s11 V1: answering a declined question from acquired documents ships OFF until the router returns a category enum (owner decision OD-1, P1.8). When true, only an off-domain (never deny/injection/malformed) decline whose ACQUIRED-only corpus admits >= admission thresholds is answered.

search._arxiv_off_note: CONTROL-GAPS-1107 ARXIV-OFF: off because export.arxiv.org robots.txt disallows / for all agents and arxiv.org disallows /api; interim until the owner decides (H-1). "arxiv" removed from search.providers; restore it together with search.arxiv.enabled in vera_eval_run.json. arxiv_route (abs/html/pdf full text) is unchanged and stays on.
search._providers_note: plan D-3 + s11 V9, updated NONASK-1103 WP-F0: openalex and arxiv (ARX-A2 supersedes "Europe PMC refuses preprints": the arxiv_route fetches CC-licensed arXiv HTML; remove "arxiv" to restore openalex only). arXiv is called once per job, separately from OpenAlex (OpenAlex results are all kept), counted in bounds.max_search_calls_per_job; its candidates rank in tier 1 only while arxiv_route.enabled is true; the licence is still decided at fetch. This applies only to this providers list. DuckDuckGo (ddg_first.enabled), Europe PMC and the Wikipedia reference portal run concurrently in acquisition search (vera/search_providers.py acquisition_search); a DDG result still becomes a candidate only via a scholarly identifier. openalex_profile._note: ACQ-SEARCH-1021 (acquisition only; /ask unchanged). filter: OpenAlex works held by PubMed Central (source S2764455111), the only place Europe PMC full text comes from. and_extra_max/generic_terms: when the question has no core phrase, AND the distinctive terms instead of OR-ing every token (OR let ambiguous 'mma' match alpha-gal papers). No model call. Remove the block to restore the previous query.

subquery._calibration_note: SHIPS FLAG-OFF (orchestrator decision after round-2 label review, 2026-11-03). The code, the registry disambiguation (config/entity_registry.json full_aliases, parents, context_terms, generic_phrases) and both fixture files (tests/fixtures/nonask_1103/subquery_search.json, subquery_adversarial.json) are kept. Round-2 skeptic probes: 8 of 15 fresh off-entity probes still reached tier 0 and 5 of 13 relevant probes dropped; the registry's generic phrases copy the fixture. Enabling requires ALL of: (1) a holdout written independently of the registry curator; (2) relevant records that use the plain entity name; (3) context terms that are not the question's own words; (4) real-data calibration (plan 5b), not synthetic fixtures. Offline replay figures (adversarial holdout off-entity tier 0 7/7 to 0/7, relevant 12/12 to 12/12) are fitted to the curator's own probes and are NOT evidence for enabling.
subquery._note: NONASK-1103 S3 (plan work/NONASK-1103/subquery-plan.md 6.2). Inline acquisition only. When vera.subquery splits the question into n >= 2 parts, OpenAlex, Europe PMC and arXiv run once per part (the named entity central in each query), inside bounds.max_search_calls_per_job scaled to 7 + 3*(n-1) (16 for 4 parts; vera.search_providers.subquery_budget): a RECORDED LOOSENING of an existing budget (OD-1027 p3), not a new cap. The question-level slots (Wikipedia, id lookup, OpenAlex OR retry, the one DDG call) are reserved first. One job reservation per question; rate gates unchanged. Kill switch: false restores the single search. Shipped FALSE (see _calibration_note); live 429 behaviour and latency UNTESTED.

ddg_first._note: YIELD-1021 (owner 2026-10-21: "ddg should be the first source for prompts/queries that are not in the corpus"). Acquisition and inline only. The shared /ask DuckDuckGoLiteProvider (its cache, daily_query_cap and gate, config search.duckduckgo_lite in vera_eval_run.json) runs concurrently with OpenAlex and Europe PMC; a result becomes a candidate ONLY via a scholarly identifier (DOI in the URL, PMC/PubMed link via one Europe PMC id lookup, arXiv id, or the citation_doi meta tag of a portal landing page fetched once, public-address checked, <= landing_max_bytes, <= landing_timeout_s, at most max_landing_fetches) and then passes the UNCHANGED resolve, fetch and licence gates; DDG-mapped candidates rank first. Every other page is held (never ingested or used as evidence). Planner priors, uncalibrated. enabled=false restores the previous search.

europepmc.query_suffix: OPEN_ACCESS:y AND HAS_FT:y AND NOT SRC:PPR AND NOT LICENSE:"cc by-nd" AND NOT LICENSE:"cc by-nc-nd"
europepmc._note: YIELD-1021: second metadata search, acquisition only (never the /ask reading list): Europe PMC lite search for open-access works with Europe PMC full text, merged with OpenAlex de-duplicated by DOI or PMCID; hits still resolve through the unchanged resolve_oa (by DOI; PLAN-NONDOI-1022: hits without a DOI resolve by PMCID, and only hits with neither are R-ACQ-NODOI). One search call. enabled=false removes it.

search._openalex_quota_note: YIELD-1021: after an OpenAlex HTTP 429 / budget error (keyless free tier = a small daily budget shared per IP, observed exhausted 2026-10-21 by BENCH-1021 and this task's live check) the acquisition search skips OpenAlex for this many seconds (process-wide; DDG and Europe PMC still run; the job makes one OpenAlex attempt, max_retries 1, so no Retry-After sleep). Planner prior, uncalibrated: lower it once a key (optional env OPENALEX_API_KEY, never logged) is set. Counted as openalex_429 / openalex_skipped_quota in the 'autoacq sources' log line.
search._results_per_provider_note: OD-1031-SHORTLIST31 follow-up (2026-10-31): 10 -> 31 (and europepmc.page_size 10 -> 31) so ONE request per provider can supply up to 31 candidates for the 31-candidate shortlist. No extra calls: max_search_calls_per_job and max_calls_per_provider_per_job are unchanged, and rate limits are unchanged. It is the per_page of the one OpenAlex call (and its OR retry), the max_results of arXiv when enabled, and the n passed to DuckDuckGo and the Wikipedia portal (which have their own caps). Documented provider maxima, from memory and UNVERIFIED here: OpenAlex per_page up to 200; Europe PMC REST pageSize up to 1000; arXiv API max_results up to 2000 per request (30000 total). NOT calibrated on live data: response sizes (europepmc max_response_bytes 2000000 applies) and latency at 31 per page are unmeasured. grounding.num_results (config/ask-provider-chain.json) is the /ask reading-list size, not this value, and does not clip the acquisition search.
search._max_calls_per_provider_per_job_note: NONASK-1103 WP-F0: read by no code in this repository version (not enforced); the per-job call counts are set by bounds.max_search_calls_per_job. No new cap.

freshness._note: FRESH-1023, amended FRESH-AMEND-1023 (owner clarification 2026-10-23, verbatim: "there should be a date stamp for when a chunk is added to the corpus. that is the date that should be used for freshness testing. there should separately be a date stamp for each chunk's source creation/authoring"). Trigger basis = corpus_added_at (per chunk: evidence_spans.created_at, else sources.created_at, else provenance.retrieved_at written by the corpus writer on the vera.freshness.utcnow clock): older than freshness_max_age_hours -> 'stale'; missing, partial (year/month/date-only), unparseable or future -> 'freshness_unknown' AND revised to the request's now() (vera.corpus_stamp: in memory, and a conditional single-row UPDATE through the WO app path when VERA_DB_URL_WO is set). source_authored_at (published/updated metadata, precision year|month|day) drives ONLY the older/recent label (sources[].evidence_recency): a partial authored date is 'older' only when its whole period ended more than freshness_max_age_hours ago, else 'unknown'; it is never 'recent' (source_authored_partial_dates_trusted false -> partial = 'unknown'). A newly added old publication therefore does not trigger freshness research but is labelled older. freshness_max_age_hours 24 is OWNER-SPECIFIED, not calibrated. UNCALIBRATED planner priors (calibration rule): freshness_future_skew_seconds 300, source_authored_partial_dates_trusted true, sufficiency.partial_is_insufficient true. What would change them: live research.outcome, freshness counts and backfill counts. enabled=false restores the previous behaviour.
freshness._always_acquire_new_note: OD-1109-SIX (owner 2026-11-09, verbatim: "ingest at least 6 new documents found from external search results, including from following links from portals until arriving at original hosts of sources"). Exactly true: every grounded answer also runs the existing research attempt (trigger new_documents; one inline acquisition per request, its rounds aiming at bounds.acq_round_target_new_docs NEW documents, i.e. reused stored documents do not count unless bounds.acq_round_count_reused is true), bounded by the unchanged deadline, job quota and the per-prompt ceiling (max_docs_per_prompt), then answers from stored + new evidence; texts.new_documents states how many new were obtained. Fewer than the target is a resource limitation, never a reason not to answer. false restores the previous trigger rule (insufficient / stale / unknown only).

texts.new_documents_quota: No new search was possible for this question this hour: VERA-DAR's limit on new searches has been reached, so this answer uses only the documents it already holds.
texts.new_documents: VERA-DAR searched for new sources for this question and obtained {n} new full document{s} (it aims for at least {m}).
texts.fresh_new: Freshness: {n_new} cited document(s) were found by a new search for this question; cited documents published within the last 24 hours: {n_fresh}; published earlier: {n_stale}; publication time not precise enough to tell: {n_unknown}. Documents are dated by publication, not by when VERA-DAR added them to its collection.
texts.mixed_ages: Older and newly found sources are both cited and labelled by publication date; where they differ, the more recent publication is not automatically correct, and an older publication is not current because VERA-DAR obtained it today.
texts.new_evidence_unanswered: A new search found full-text sources, but no checked answer could be written from them, so this answer uses the earlier sources only.

bounds._jobs_per_hour_note: OD-1109-QUOTA (owner 2026-11-09, Raise the quota): 30 -> 120, because OD-1109-SIX runs a new-document search (one job per round) on every answered question. An owner-set resource bound, not calibrated; when it is still exhausted the answer says so (freshness.texts.new_documents_quota). What would change it: live hourly job use per question.
bounds._docs_per_day_note: OWNER DECISION 2026-10-22 (verbatim, relayed by the orchestrator to DAR-TRACE-1022): "abolish the 20-a-day limit". null = no daily document cap (vera.acq_config.docs_per_day_cap); the RO daily count is not read. Still bounded by jobs_per_hour 30, jobs_per_day 180 and max_docs_per_job 2 (at most 360 documents/day; was 6/30/2 = 60 before OD-1031-PROMPTLIM). A number restores the cap.
bounds._max_search_calls_note: NONASK-1103 WP-F0: 6 -> 7 adds the arXiv call (providers includes "arxiv"), taken after Europe PMC and Wikipedia and before the id lookup, so lookup_left stays 1 (the Europe PMC id lookup and the Europe PMC OR retry still run). This loosens an existing budget; it adds no new cap. YIELD-1021: 2 -> 5 = OpenAlex 2 (AND profile + OR retry) + DuckDuckGo 1 + Europe PMC 1 + Europe PMC id lookup for DDG PMC/PubMed links 1. A lower value drops the later ones in that order (vera.search_providers.acquisition_search). INT-1022-B (orchestrator disposition 2026-10-22, owner may override): 5 -> 6 adds ONE slot for the Wikipedia reference portal (config/wiki_ref_portal.json; identifiers only, never evidence), taken after Europe PMC and before the id lookup, so the lookup keeps its slot (DAR-TRACE-1022's Europe PMC OR retry shares the lookup slot). This is an outbound search budget, not an acquisition cap: every candidate still passes the unchanged resolve, licence, injection, relevance and admission gates. Calibration: work/wikiref-1022/INTEGRATION.md 'Observed shapes', 3 live sample questions on 2026-10-22: the portal used 1 MediaWiki request each (0.4-0.65 s, one sample each), within its own budget.max_requests_per_question 4; candidates 20/0/2 (all DOI). Not a latency or yield calibration (3 samples). What would change it: 'autoacq sources' wiki_raw and cand_wikipedia_portal counts and the per-portal ratelimit log over a week of live jobs (drop back to 5 if the portal adds no stored documents).
bounds._max_candidates_resolved_note: owner decision OD-1031-SHORTLIST31 (2026-10-31): shortlist ceiling 6 -> 31 candidates (rank_candidates cut, vera/auto_acquire.py). This note covers only the shortlist size. Other limits changed by their own owner decisions: the per-prompt document ceiling max_docs_per_prompt 31 (OD-1031-CEIL31; inline_fresh_docs is retired from the shipped config) and the job caps jobs_per_hour 30 and jobs_per_day 180 (OD-1031-PROMPTLIM). Unchanged here: max_docs_per_job (background, 2), max_search_calls_per_job, inline.deadline_s, per_doc_timeout_s, fetch timeouts and rate limits are unchanged. CALIBRATION (repo/CLAUDE.md rule): NOT yet calibrated on live data. Source = the owner decision. Real data available: the P1 funnel (32 candidates found, 26 not shortlisted under the old cut of 6; work/P1-DIAG-1031/PLAN.md:54, relayed) and the 2026-10-21 local timings (work/dar-inline-1021/e2e/logs: inline total 5.3 s and 6.3 s, fetch+gates 3.5/4.8 s for 2 documents; one topic, stubbed LLMs). Spread seen: one funnel, two timing runs. Why 31: owner rationale (verbatim): "I settled upon 31 because that's over the 30 minimum needed for statistical descriptiveness." (it is also one below the 32 found in that funnel). What would change it: the metadata probe (work/P1-PROBE-1031) and live per-candidate resolve/fetch timings and the share of candidates reached before inline.deadline_s 45 (autoacq inline ms_* lines).
bounds._acq_round_count_reused_note: OD-1109-SIX: already-stored documents re-found by a search are not new and do not count toward acq_round_target_new_docs (or toward round progress). true restores the pre-SIX count.
bounds._acq_round_count_kinds_note: MIDTERMS-WP10-1106 (owner OD-1106-MIDTERMS-D1D4, D3; vera/evidence_ledger.py): the source kinds whose qualifying (passed the existing admission, thresholds unchanged), deduplicated, full- or partial-text examined sources count toward acq_round_target_new_docs. Metadata-only, duplicate and examined-but-unqualified sources never count. web is kept because the target already counted web pages read; removing it narrows the count to D3's literal three kinds. Same as the code default. Not a threshold.
bounds._acq_round_max_open_note: ROUNDS-1028: upper bound on simultaneously open per-topic acquisition rounds held in process (vera/acq_rounds.py); beyond it the least recently updated open round is evicted (its count is lost; DV-ACQ-FLOOR6-1 family). A memory bound, not a decision threshold, and no cap, admission or serving effect.
bounds._acq_round_target_note: FLOOR6-1028 INTERIM (vera/acq_rounds.py; owner 2026-10-28 verbatim: "Really, it should be: as each round of topic addition (initial or subsequent) should target at least 6 new docs. If there simply are not 6 more new docs to be found, that's a resource limitation, not a process failure."; OD-1027(4)). Every acquisition round for a micro-topic targets at least this many NEW stored documents; outcome met (>= target) or resource_limited (routes exhausted below target; not an error). Job caps unchanged (jobs_per_hour 6, jobs_per_day 30, max_docs_per_job 2), so a round of 6 spans >= 3 jobs. 6 is owner-declared, NOT calibrated (plan s24 Wilson note: half-width <= 0.10 at p 0.75 needs n about 70). Round state is in-process only (lost on restart) until the 010 acq_jobs table carries a round field; wired observationally by ROUNDS-1028 (topic key = read-time micro_topic anchor key, else unassigned; DV-ACQ-FLOOR6-1).
bounds._served_topic_balanced_note: FLOOR6-1028 (owner 2026-10-28, verbatim: "btw, 6 docs isn't a ceiling, it's a floor. statistically, 3/5 is only 60%, and 1/5 is only 20%. we need the tails smaller and the middle closer to 65%-85%"; corrected the same day: "Really, it should be: as each round of topic addition (initial or subsequent) should target at least 6 new docs. If there simply are not 6 more new docs to be found, that's a resource limitation, not a process failure."; OD-1027(4)). Serving has NO per-topic ceiling: served_per_topic_max null; served_topic_balanced true keeps the topic-balanced ORDER (round-robin across read-time micro-topic keys, topics by newest member, newest first within a topic, an unkeyed row its own topic), so only the global totals bind (served_acquired_max 30, served_acquired_max_bytes 50000000; raising them is an owner decision, work/acq-1027/plan.md s24). The 6 applies to ACQUISITION rounds (acq_round_target_new_docs), not to serving. Rollback: served_per_topic_max 6 restores the A4 ceiling; served_topic_balanced false with a null ceiling restores newest-N.
bounds._served_per_topic_note: SUPERSEDED in part by FLOOR6-1028 (_served_topic_balanced_note: no per-topic ceiling). ACQ S4-0 L9 (PD-1, G-SERVE). Serve the acquired corpus per micro-topic instead of the newest N by source_id: at most this many documents per read-time micro-topic key (vera.micro_topic), taken round-robin across topics newest topic first, total still capped by served_acquired_max / served_acquired_max_bytes (rebuild cost unchanged). A document with no assignable key counts as its own topic. null or absent = the previous newest-N behaviour (rollback). CAP6-1028: 3 -> 6 on the basis of owner declaration OD-1027(4) (records/decisions.md): "for statistical analysis, we really need at least 6 docs per micro-topic" (supersedes the S4-0 planner prior of 3, which was PROVISIONAL, DV-ACQ-6 family). Real-data state 2026-10-28: 63 stored documents in total; the per-micro-topic distribution is UNMEASURED (owner-run count pending, G0), so this is an owner-declared requirement, NOT a calibrated threshold. Interaction: the total caps are unchanged (served_acquired_max 30, served_acquired_max_bytes 50000000), so raising the per-topic cap adds no rebuild cost; round-robin still gives every topic its first document before any topic its second, so at most 30 / 6 = 5 topics can reach 6 served documents at once, and with 63 stored documents at most 30 are served. A topic with fewer than 6 stored documents is served in full. What would change it: the per-key document counts of the stored rows (owner-authorised SELECT) showing how many topics hold >= 6 documents, rebuild timing at the cap, and any owner decision to raise served_acquired_max (incremental indexing, plan OM-4, needed beyond about 50 documents).
bounds._served_scan_note: L9: at most this many newest acquired rows are indexed (source_id and provenance only, no content) to choose what to serve; a bound, not a decision threshold.
bounds._max_docs_per_prompt_note: owner decision OD-1031-CEIL31 (2026-10-31: "limit new source fulltext ingestions to 31 per prompt", "min 6, max 31"): fresh-document budget of ONE live (inline) prompt, replacing bounds.inline_fresh_docs (retired). Background jobs keep bounds.max_docs_per_job 2. One inline prompt is still ONE job against jobs_per_hour/jobs_per_day; inline.deadline_s 45 still bounds the pass (its removal is gated with STREAM-1031); the daily-budget logic (docs_per_day, null = none) still applies; no licence, injection, relevance or persist_min_admitted_spans gate is relaxed; persistence stays insert-only, one transaction per document through the WoStore. Owner rationale (verbatim): "I settled upon 31 because that's over the 30 minimum needed for statistical descriptiveness." CALIBRATION: NOT calibrated on live data. Source = the owner decision. Active while inline.per_prompt_ceiling_enabled is true (shipped true; kill switch). Worst case 180 prompts/day x 31 = 5,580 persisted documents/day (OD-1031-NO500). Real data: 2026-10-21 local runs fetched 2 documents in 3.5-4.8 s (work/dar-inline-1021/e2e/logs); no measurement exists of 31 parallel fetches. With fetch_workers 4 and per_doc_timeout_s 25 at most 4 documents are in flight, so the 45 s deadline, not this number, will usually end the pass. What would change it: live inline ms_* timings, admitted-per-prompt and persist counts, Europe PMC 429/skip share.
bounds._jobs_per_hour_day_note: owner decision OD-1031-PROMPTLIM (2026-10-31, verbatim: "the hourly prompt limit should be 30. the per day should be 180"): jobs_per_hour 6 -> 30 and jobs_per_day 30 -> 180 (shared by inline acquisition and background jobs). Owner values; NOT calibrated: no live traffic or job-rate data exists. max_docs_per_job 2, queue_max 4 and BG_MIN_FREE_HOURLY_JOBS 2 are unchanged, so the unattended ceiling is now 180 jobs x 2 documents = 360 documents/day (was 60). What would change it: live autoacq job counts per hour/day, the openalex/europepmc ratelimit log lines and 429 share, and the stored-document yield per job.
bounds._answer_min_admitted_spans_note: ONE-SPAN-1021 (owner approval 2026-10-21, DAR single-passage answer eligibility): on the inline answer path a fetched document with >= this many qualifying passages (after the unchanged licence, integrity, injection, harmful-content and relevance checks) supplies evidence to the EPHEMERAL answer corpus of this request only. Every sentence is still claim-checked against its cited passage and removed when unsupported; a partly covered question is answered as partial (claim_check.answer_completeness). Code floor 1 (0 qualifying passages never answers: reading list). Calibration: same data as _min_admitted_spans_note (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json, 9 real DAR-9 texts): at >= 1 span on-topic passes 7 of 17 (vs 5 at >= 2), off-topic false passes 2.6% (vs 2.2%), off-corpus probes 14.8% (vs 7.4%). Value 1 is the owner decision; the higher probe false-pass rate is bounded by the per-claim check (unsupported sentences removed) and by not persisting such documents. Change it when live ACQ-ANSWER-ONLY counts and reviewed single-passage answers show the per-claim check does not contain the false passes.
bounds._persist_min_admitted_spans_note: ONE-SPAN-1021: persistent-corpus admission, unchanged value (was min_admitted_spans; the calibration note below applies). A document below it may answer the request (answer_min_admitted_spans) but is NOT written (telemetry persisted=false, reason below_persist_min). The background job persists only at >= this value. Code floor 2 (owner).
bounds._min_admitted_spans_note: (applies to persist_min_admitted_spans) calibration 2026-10-21 (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json): single-document admission over the 9 real DAR-9 texts. calset-v2 on-topic (question, source doc) pairs: 17, of which >=1 span 7, >=2 5, >=3 4. Off-topic pairs (calset question vs other doc): 230, >=1 6 (2.6%), >=2 5 (2.2%), >=3 2 (0.9%). B2 off-corpus probes x 9 docs: 54, >=1 8 (14.8%), >=2 4 (7.4%), >=3 3 (5.6%). Value 2: halves the probe false-pass rate of 1 at a cost of 2 of 7 on-topic passes; 3 loses another on-topic pass for a small further gain. The gate is conservative (most on-topic pairs admit 0 spans) and not clean (2-7% false passes): residual R-7/FM-13. Change it when live R-ACQ-FEWSPANS/IRRELEVANT counts and stored-document reviews show a different trade-off.
bounds._served_acquired_max_note: measured 2026-10-21 (work/wed-acq2/measure/measure-out.json, measure2-out.json; dev machine, CPU only): acquired-corpus rebuild = verify + DarCorpus index 20 docs 64.5 s + evidence index 63.3 s; 30 docs 75.9 s + 77.5 s; 50 docs 141 s; 100 docs 230 s (index only). inline._doc: DAR-INLINE-1021: inline acquisition inside the /ask request, off-topic override path only (vera/inline_acquire.py). Counts against bounds.jobs_per_hour, jobs_per_day and docs_per_day; uses max_candidates_resolved, max_docs_per_job and fetch_timeout_s unchanged; answers at bounds.answer_min_admitted_spans and persists at bounds.persist_min_admitted_spans (ONE-SPAN-1021). enabled=false restores the background-only behaviour.
inline._in_scope_note: DAR-INLINE-1021-R2 must-have 1: an IN-SCOPE question whose full-document result is insufficient or corpus_unusable (including while the base warm-up runs, must-have 2) also acquires inline, through the same gates, caps, kill switch and claim check; the answer uses the normal in-scope wording (no off-topic prefix). Layer-1 denies and injection hits never acquire. false = in-scope keeps the background trigger only.
inline._persist_deadline_note: RETRIEVAL-1109 H-4 (owner OD-1109-RETRIEVAL, approved 2026-11-09 as relayed by the coordinator; switch: persist_extends_deadline, exactly true = on, false = the 45 s deadline for every request). A keep-searching request (vera.request_intent persist) on the NON-streamed path gets inline deadline_s = persist_deadline_max_s (vera.ask_service.persist_acq); the streamed path has no inline deadline and is unaffected. Calibration note for 100: it is the most the existing request budget can give the inline pass anyway: public_mode.ASK_TIMEOUT_S 180 minus the post-inline tail ask_service.inline_need_s (3 LLM calls x chain timeout_s 20 + 2 reading-list searches x grounding deadline_s 10 = 80). The request budget still bounds every round (secs = remaining - tail), so the value can never outlast the client's wait. Measured on: config arithmetic only (no live latency); at Europe PMC's 10 s spacing (rate_limits.json, Crawl-delay 10) 100 s holds about 3 more full-text requests than 45 s. What would change it: ASK_TIMEOUT_S, the chain timeout, or live 'autoacq inline' ms_total for persist requests.
inline._variant_lane_note: RETRIEVAL-1109 A3 (NOANSWER-ROOT-1109 plan A3; kill switch, false = round 0 only as before): for a news-intent question (vera.news_intent) each variant round (rounds 2+) on the STREAMED path (the lane's own timeouts and GDELT spacing are not bounded by the non-streamed deadline, so that path is unchanged) also runs ONE reporting-lane pass with the variant text (vera.inline_acquire._variant_lane -> lane_evidence.collect). Every lane rule applies unchanged: GDELT min_interval_s/backoff/circuit/daily caps, outlet verdicts, ND link-only unless nc_basis SATISFIED and licence_rules nd_news enabled (then answer-only, never stored), robots and page signals. Pages are answer-only, request-local and count toward the round target. No new number.
inline._acq6_no_progress_note: Safety bound (orchestrator 2026-11-04): the round loop stops (stop=no_progress) after 2 consecutive variant rounds with zero new usable (answer-eligible) documents (vera.inline_acquire.NO_PROGRESS_ROUNDS, a structural constant with its calibration note there; not tunable here).
inline._web_read_note: NONASK-1103 A6-W (owner R-045/R-047/R-048/R-050, review N3/N4): kill switch for the answer-only web route (vera.web_route over the round-0 general-web results; read gate before any fetch via vera.source_permissions, vera.public_fetch only, one fetch per host, use_for_answer gate, never stored, cached, queued or logged). Ships true by owner decision; false = no web route (pre-A6-W). No threshold added.
inline._acq6_rounds_note: NONASK-1103 A6 D1 (owner R-045; plan work/NONASK-1103/acq6-plan.md s4, spec D1; vera/inline_acquire._extra_rounds). ROLE: when the first search leaves fewer than acq_round_target_new_docs (6) answer-eligible documents (fresh + reused + answer-only/lane pages) and its ranked list is exhausted, take the next query variant (vera/query_variants6.py over vera/query_variants_acq.py; finite list, never the raw sentence; seeds in config/acq_variants.json) and search again. One job reservation per round (rounds 2+ also refuse below the 2-free-hourly-jobs background floor); tried keys are never re-evaluated; documents found only by a variant query are ANSWER-ONLY (never stored or cached) until the G1 topic anchor is calibrated. Streamed path: no wall-clock bound (OD-1031-NODEADLINE), bounded by the finite variant list, the job floor, stall_s, disconnect checks and per-fetch timeouts. Non-stream path: deadline_s 45 is an absolute bound across rounds with the per_doc_timeout_s fetch reserve every round. false = KILL SWITCH: exactly the previous single search. UNCALIBRATED: no live data on documents reached per added round or on latency (6 texts in 45 s is not demonstrated); calibrate from the logged rounds/stop telemetry (Outcome.acquisition rounds, stop).
inline._per_prompt_ceiling_note: OD-1031-CEIL31 + OD-1031-NO500 (2026-10-31): true (default) = a live (inline) prompt may take up to bounds.max_docs_per_prompt (31) fresh documents; false = KILL SWITCH restoring the previous 2-documents-per-job behaviour (bounds.max_docs_per_job). The earlier default-off gating (OD-1031-HITL4, pending a database-backed 500/day cap) was dropped when the owner removed the 500/day cap (OD-1031-NO500). Worst case now: jobs_per_day 180 x 31 = 5,580 persisted documents/day (inline prompts), plus background jobs at max_docs_per_job 2 sharing the same 180 jobs/day. Uncalibrated; no live data on documents persisted per prompt.
inline._discovered_max_note: owner decision OD-1031-SHORTLIST31 (2026-10-31): 6 -> 31 so discovered_max does not clip below bounds.max_candidates_resolved (see its _max_candidates_resolved_note for the calibration status: NOT yet calibrated on live data). Not the effective limit today: grounding.num_results is 5 (config/ask-provider-chain.json:52), so at most 5 discovered records are offered.
inline._p0_5_note: P0-5-ACQ (owner decisions D1-D5, 2026-10-22; vera/acq_discovered.py). use_discovered SHIPS ON (owner decisions D3/D5, 2026-10-23, Demo Day enablement; kill switch VERA_AUTOACQ_DISABLED); landing_route ships off and enabling it is a separate owner decision. use_discovered: the request's own cached discovery results (reading-list search) also become acquisition candidates (index licence dropped; deterministic Gate A; unchanged resolve/fetch/licence/injection/relevance/admission gates; per-record outcome in inline_acquisition.discovered; provenance.acquisition.discovery/url_chain/gate_a/gate_b/retention). landing_route (needs use_discovered): ONE bounded DOI -> landing -> JATS XML attempt within the landing_route host allowlists when Europe PMC has no open-access record. discovered_max 31 (was 6, OD-1031-SHORTLIST31): a candidate-count cap equal to bounds.max_candidates_resolved (planner prior, not a decision threshold; uncalibrated: no live run of this path exists; change it from live 'discovered' outcome counts).
inline._reuse_note: DAR-INLINE-1021-R2: ranked candidates already stored as acquired documents (and not tried by the stored-corpus attempt) are answered from their stored rows, read-only, re-verified at read (marker, every JATS licence element, injection re-scan, hashes) and never re-fetched or re-stored; they fill max_docs_per_job first and are not capped by docs_per_day (nothing new is acquired). DAR-TRACE-1022: a reused row must first pass THIS question's per-document relevance gate (answer_min_admitted_spans, same admission as a fresh document); a failing row is counted R-ACQ-REUSE-IRRELEVANT (R-ACQ-REUSE-UNUSABLE when the reader refuses it), does not use up max_docs_per_job and is not re-acquired. The previous accepted divergence (no relevance gate on reuse) is closed.
inline._calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED against live. deadline_s 45 covers search through the parallel fetch and gates; persist (measured 0.06 s; statement_timeout 15 s per statement) and the ephemeral corpus build (0.08-0.3 s) run after it. CMF-1022 retry guard (ask_service.inline_need_s): ONE request-level deadline (handler entry + public_mode.ASK_TIMEOUT_S 180 s, shared by every provider of the chain, at most one inline search per request) and the in-scope inline RETRY starts only if remaining >= deadline_s 45 + 3 x chain timeout_s 20 (writer + claim check + a second claim-check call) + 2 x grounding deadline_s 10 (reading-list fallback) = 125 s (this equals the worst path below, excluding the classifier already spent); an unreadable term skips the retry (inline_acquisition status budget_unknown), a short budget skips it (status deadline). The 15 s margin is not applied (180 s, not 165 s). RESIDUAL GAP: the 180 s is enforced only by the client; the server does not terminate a request. Budget against the UI's 180 s timeout with a 15 s margin (165 s): classifier <= 20 s (ask-provider-chain timeout_s) + inline <= 45 s + answer writer <= 20 s + claim check <= 20 s per call + reading-list fallback <= 2 x 10 s (grounding deadline_s, rl3 AND then OR) = 125 s worst single-call path, leaving 40 s for a second claim-check call. Measured locally 2026-10-21 (work/dar-inline-1021/e2e/logs/stage_inline_run1.json, run2.json; isolated PG16, real OpenAlex + Europe PMC, classifier/answer/claim-check LLM stubbed; boxing/MMA question): inline total 5.3 s and 6.3 s (search 1.5/1.2 s, parallel fetch+gates 3.5/4.8 s, write 0.06 s, ephemeral corpus 0.15/0.08 s). So 45 s is about 7x the measured cold path; lower it when live 'autoacq inline' ms_total lines show the spread, raise it only with the budget above. per_doc_timeout_s 25 (>= fetch_timeout_s 20 plus resolve), fetch_workers 4 (evaluate up to max_candidates_resolved 31 at once, admit at most bounds.max_docs_per_prompt 31 per live prompt when inline.per_prompt_ceiling_enabled is true, else max_docs_per_job 2; OD-1031-CEIL31), max_concurrent 2 (server-wide inline acquisitions; CPU-light, network-bound; planner prior), max_waiters 4 and waiter_wait_s 45 (identical in-flight questions; = deadline), result_ttl_s 600 (outcome reuse for provider-chain retries and repeats until the background refresh serves the stored documents): planner priors, not decision gates.

live._note: STREAM-1031 (streamed POST /ask/stream path only; legacy /ask never reads these): bounds replacing the removed 45 s inline cut (OD-1031-NODEADLINE). stall_s = seconds with no progress event (candidate evaluated, document stored) before the prompt stops (status resource_limited, stop stalled) and persists what it admitted. max_reuse_checks_per_prompt = the most stored-document reuse checks one prompt runs when the deadline no longer bounds them. persist_timeout_s = documentation of the per-document persist bound; it MUST equal db_statement_timeout_ms / 1000 (a test asserts it) and enforces nothing by itself.
live._calibration_note: PROVISIONAL, unmeasured; no live data at these values. stall_s 300 is a prior: the longest single bounded step between progress events is a search rung of 6 calls x (20 s search timeout + 2 s rate-limit wait) + 3 x 5 s landing = 147 s, or one arXiv document 50 s, so 300 s is about 2x the longest expected gap; spread unknown. Source: owner decision OD-1031-HITL4 item 4 (approve a 300 s no-progress cutoff provided total work is also bounded by finite steps, requests, tokens and cost). Change it from the live p99 gap between progress events; lower it if users abandon first, raise it only if stalled stops fire on runs that later progress. max_reuse_checks_per_prompt 31 = bounds.max_docs_per_prompt (owner decision OD-1031-CEIL31, 31 per prompt = the shortlist, OD-1031-SHORTLIST31; not duplicated here as a separate limit source); change it with that ceiling. persist_timeout_s 15 = db_statement_timeout_ms 15000 (existing). T_max derivation: work/STREAM-1031/PLAN.md s2.6.

micro_topic._note: ACQ S4-0 L2/L2b. Read-time micro-topic key only; nothing is written (PD-3). anchor_bm25 is a PROVISIONAL prior (plan DV-ACQ-6), NOT calibrated: the frozen 200-document reference sample does not exist offline (no raw sources in the repo), so the IDF snapshot is built from the anchor texts only; a mis-assigned key only changes which stored documents are served first, never the total cap. k5.enabled false: no question-derived query leaves in S4-0.

judge._note: TOPICJUDGE-1028 (OD-1028(54): G2, live calibration; OD-1028(57): shadow never blocks). OFF by default (enabled must be literally true, and registration_enabled must be true too). A free Groq model (vera.inference_chain free entries, price 0 only) judges the draft against EVERY active/retired topic (no shortlist, no candidate-count cap; refused-category placeholder rows are never candidates, OD-1028(56)), run BEFORE the advisory lock, in batches of batch_size. COST GROWS WITH REGISTRY SIZE: ceil(candidates / batch_size) calls per registration; candidates beyond max_calls_per_registration or max_tokens_per_registration get the verdict unknown and the coverage (judged of total) is logged. Raise the budgets as the registry grows. mode shadow (default once enabled) AND judge disabled: registration follows the S3 rule: an exact duplicate (same normalized key, or same normalized label as an active/retired/suspended/draft topic) writes nothing and returns state duplicate, anything else is activated; the judge verdicts (shadow, logged to vera_vjay.topreg_judgments for calibration) and the lexical similarity score are LOG-ONLY and never suspend or block. mode active: yes = suspended, all no = active, any unknown or topics changed during the call = stays draft (re-proposing the key re-judges the draft); the lexical stand-in is log-only. Every failure (timeout, refusal-shaped, malformed output, budget) = unknown. max_judgments_per_day is reserved under a short lock before any call (reservation rows). These are the judge OWN allowances: max_groq_tokens_per_job (0) caps acquisition jobs and is untouched. All numbers are PROVISIONAL, uncalibrated, and the live model behaviour is UNTESTED.

registry_table._note: TOPICREG-1028 (owner: a table means a database table). read_from_db: explicit true reads vera_vjay.topreg_topics (db/migrations/pending/011-DRAFT, NOT applied) and uses only state=active rows; the JSON seed is used only when to_regclass says the table is absent; any other DB error or an invalid table stops (fail closed). registration_enabled: explicit true lets vera.topic_registry.register_proposed_topic write a draft, then, unless the judge is in ACTIVE mode, applies the S3 rule (OD-1028(57)): an exact duplicate returns state duplicate and writes nothing, anything else becomes active. The lexical similarity score (similarity_max 0.50, PROVISIONAL; scope_router.description_similarity, stemmed Jaccard plus char trigrams, LEXICAL NOT SEMANTIC) is LOG-ONLY and never suspends. In judge ACTIVE mode the judge verdicts decide (see judge._note). A MATCH = semantic equivalence or paraphrase only; narrower or broader non-equivalent topics are distinct (OD-1028(49)). Default OFF. refused_state_map (PROVISIONAL, OD-1028(51)/(52)/(56)): object, refusal category code -> refused state, used by vera.topic_registry.ensure_refused_category (fixed placeholder rows only, no question text) and scrutiny_flag (category level only). Validated at load: every key must be a classifier category whose disposition is refuse, every value one of banned/prohibited/secrets. No code maps to secrets (secrets is admin-only) until a real secret-leak refusal code exists. Such rows are never loaded as active, never trigger acquisition and are never text-matched. app_roles (D11): the three group and three login role names that the 011 draft's psql-variable defaults also use (app_rw_login, app_wo_login, app_ro_login); validated at load; an -v override of those variables must be mirrored here. cache_ttl_seconds (accepted 0..3600, else rejected at load): how long the DB registry (or the absent-table fallback) is cached before it is re-read. proposal_state: app-proposed topics are written as draft (the DB trigger enforces it); only draft is accepted.

Exact host names only (no wildcards, no suffix matching), re-checked on every hop with https, no userinfo, port 443, the public-address check and robots.txt (fail closed). resolver_hosts are the DOI resolver; publisher_hosts are the owner-approved publisher hosts for landing pages AND JATS targets (the JATS URL must be on the same host as the final landing page). publisher_hosts SHIPS EMPTY: candidate hosts are pending owner sign-off after raw-HTML verification (work/demo-1022/p0-5/NOTES.md), so with the flag on and the list empty every landing route ends R-ACQ-HOST. arxiv_route._doc: ARX-A2 (vera/arxiv_fulltext.py): discovered arXiv records without a journal DOI are no longer held blindly. abs page (identity, metadata, the paper's own licence link) -> representations in order (html; pdf is recorded as not attempted: no PDF extractor exists) -> the existing HTML converter restricted to <article> -> every unchanged gate. SECURITY-CONFIG CHANGE (needs security review): hosts is the arXiv route's OWN fetch allowlist (exact host, https, checked on every redirect hop by auto_acquire._guarded_get with the public-address check and the pinned transport); fetch.allowed_hosts (Europe PMC) is not widened. Requests to arxiv.org are paced by the rate_limits.json arxiv portal (1 request / 3 s, one connection). licence_gate.py still rejects arXiv HTML (R-ACQ-ARXIV_HTML_POLICY) until the owner decides otherwise. enabled=false restores the D1 hold (R-ACQ-PREPRINT_LICENCE_UNVERIFIED).
arxiv_route._licence_note: owner decision 2026-10-23 + R1 licence rule: BY, BY-SA, BY-NC, BY-NC-SA continue to the unchanged gates; BY-ND / BY-NC-ND are rejected (ND marker, R-LIC-REJECT); anything else (arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence, CC0 as an article licence, unknown) is held R-ACQ-ARXIV_LICENCE_HOLD; no link R-ACQ-LICENCE_ABSENT; read from the requested version's abs page only (its final URL must be exactly /abs/<id><version>). ARX-SECREV-1023 R4: the BINDING family list is licence_rules.json arxiv_html_cc_families (present in config/licence_rules.json); the route admits only families in BOTH lists (arxiv_fulltext.allowed_families), so this list can never widen the gate.
arxiv_route._tdmrep_wait_note: CONTROL-GAPS-1107 r2 SAFETY BOUND, not a tuned threshold: while arxiv.org's /.well-known/tdmrep.json is not cached (same TTL as robots.txt) it is read one Crawl-delay after robots.txt, so an arXiv-routed document's per-document deadline and the inline collection window are extended by exactly one Crawl-delay, at most max_crawl_delay_s (vera/arxiv_fulltext.deadline_extension). Only the cold first document per TTL pays it (worst inline pass 45 + 15 s, inside the 40 s margin of the 165 s request budget in inline._calibration_note). Change only with max_crawl_delay_s.
arxiv_route._calibration_note: abs_max_bytes is a safety size cap, not a decision threshold: 1 MiB, uncalibrated prior (arXiv abs pages are typically tens of kB; not measured on live pages in this task, no network). Full HTML uses bounds.max_fetch_bytes unchanged. Change it from the size distribution of fetched abs pages in live logs. min_interval_s 3 = the arXiv API terms' documented one request every three seconds (rate_limits.json arxiv portal source), applied to arxiv.org too as a conservative prior; arxiv.org robots.txt was NOT read in ARX-A2 (no network): robots.txt is fetched and obeyed at run time (acq_discovered._robots_allowed, fail closed on 429/5xx/error), and a crawl-delay longer than min_interval_s is honoured; above max_crawl_delay_s 15 (a planner prior: two spaced requests must fit the 45 s inline deadline) the record is refused R-ACQ-ROBOTS rather than fetched faster. Change from the live robots.txt and 429/503 counts.

source_type_router._note: T1 (IMPL-1028-T1O1, staged Phase A, OFF). vera/source_type.py route(question) -> scholarly|general|mixed, rule-based, pure, per-request only (never stored, never identity-linked: AGENTS.md rule 1). 'general' ONLY on a general-domain lexicon hit with no scholarly signal; any ambiguity (both, neither) -> 'mixed' (fail-open). Off = route 'scholarly' behaviour: nothing changes. The target is a DB table (rows with created/modified/version and state draft/active/suspended/retired); DDL is owner-gated, so the table does not exist yet. A term ending in '*' is a token prefix; matching is on lower-cased tokens with a plural-s strip. general_ambiguous terms count only together with a general term.
source_type_router._calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED. Method: label ~60 real questions (scope_set_v1/v2 plus owner-logged live questions; question text from config/test sets only) scholarly/general/mixed by the owner or two skeptic agents on distinct models; report the confusion matrix; extend the lexicon (owner-curated) when a labelled general question falls to mixed. The costly error is general-for-scholarly; mixed is safe, only costlier. tests/test_source_type_1028.py holds a 36-question synthetic label set, which is NOT a calibration.

fit_table._note: UNCALIBRATED planner prior. kind web = DuckDuckGo-origin candidate; lower fit sorts first, AHEAD of routable_fulltext, only when topic_fit_order.enabled and the route is general or mixed. mixed is neutral (0/0): the existing order decides. Calibration: topic_fit_order._calibration_note.

topic_fit_order._note: O1 (IMPL-1028-T1O1, staged Phase A, OFF). Needs source_type_router.enabled (route general|mixed); with either off, rank_candidates is byte-for-byte today's order. When on: (1) a topic-fit key (source_type.fit) is placed AHEAD of routable_fulltext in the rank_candidates sort; (2) web_min_slots[route] of the max_candidates_resolved slots are reserved for DuckDuckGo-origin candidates (swapped in from beyond the cut, replacing the lowest-ranked non-DDG, non-protected entry); (3) web_min_reads[route] of the inline_fresh_docs reads go to the best DDG candidate. Reuse candidates (already stored: passed as `protected` keys) are never evicted and never displaced out of the fresh-read window. DP-7 caps (max_candidates_resolved, inline_fresh_docs, max_docs_per_job) are unchanged; this only reorders/swaps within them.
topic_fit_order._calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED planner priors (plan section 6). web_min_slots (of max_candidates_resolved, 6 when calibrated, now 31): real data = live dev-mode candidates[].reason/outcome for the owner-run boxing/MMA questions plus ~10 general questions; count on-topic web candidates per request and how many survive the gates; raise if web survivors are starved, lower if web slots are wasted on HOLDs. web_min_reads (of inline_fresh_docs 2): same data; compare admitted passages per read for web vs scholarly reads. mixed is 0 reads by design (SECREV C2: a misrouted scholarly question must not lose half its reads); mixed slots 0 until data justify more.

crawl_delay._note: CONTROL-GAPS-1107 r2, H-5 (approved OD-1107-HITL; see _h5_note, which supersedes the shipped-false sentence below): when enforce_on_acquisition is exactly true, the robots.txt Crawl-delay (own UA, * and AI-agent groups; vera.robots_ai.crawl_delay) of each host is honoured on auto_acquire._guarded_get and acq_discovered._b_get: a request waits until Crawl-delay seconds after the previous request to that host; a wait past the job deadline stops with R-ACQ-CRAWL_DELAY (no request sent, not an attempt). Ships false = unchanged pacing (rate_limits.json portals only; the arXiv route keeps its own Crawl-delay spacing). Not a threshold: the delay is the host's own published value.
crawl_delay._h5_note: H5-CRAWL-1107, owner OD-1107-HITL (2026-11-07) H-5(a) approved, verbatim: "Crawl-delay: Approve H-5(a), with applicable source rate restrictions enforced. Permit compliant inline acquisition and use background queues where pacing exceeds the request budget. Do not claim deferred acquisition will resolve the current question without an implemented mechanism." Ships true. Every acquisition request to a host (robots.txt, tdmrep.json, DOI landing, Europe PMC REST, full text) books the host's next slot under one lock (vera.acq_discovered.crawl_wait), so concurrent inline workers are serialized per host. Spacing = the stricter of the host's robots Crawl-delay and 1 / rate_per_s of its config/rate_limits.json portal; a host with no Crawl-delay is paced by its rate_limits.json token bucket alone. A slot past the per-document or job deadline (less min_call_s) is not booked: R-ACQ-CRAWL_DELAY, nothing sent, not an attempt, handed to the existing best-effort in-memory background queue (vera.auto_acquire.enqueue_candidates) when that queue is enabled. A server 429 on a document request is R-ACQ-RATELIMITED-THROTTLED (not an attempt; other statuses, 503 included, unchanged). Not a threshold: the delay is the host's own published value; no new cap.

repository_pdf_route._note: H20-PDF-1106 D-CFG. Flag ships OFF. Off, missing or non-boolean enabled = off; no env override. Caps and the exact-host list live in config/repository_pdf.json (required controls, PROVISIONAL values). mode answer_only: listed-host PDFs are used for answers only; ingest needs an explicit allowed licence (Q2, orchestrator 2026-11-05).
